validator: draft 1 passes with no problems, soft points or warnings
keep: The idea is named up front: a loaded generator drops voltage inside across its synchronous reactance, so E = V plus the drop, added tip to tail as on a transformer.

One rule computes every readout: drop = Xs x I at 90 degrees ahead of I, split into an across part (Xs I pf) and an along part (Xs I sine, plus lagging, minus leading); E by Pythagoras; delta from across / along; field in proportion to E with a floor at zero; AVR off, E fixed and V = sqrt(E^2 - across^2) -/+ along drop. 1.80, 56 deg, 1.25, 2.25, 32 deg, 1.20, 0.67, 0.44 and 2.24 all come from it.

Both brief misconceptions have a DO screen with their own hints: lagging and leading the wrong way round (screen 11 options; screen 6 slip 1.20) and leading is harmless (screen 8, the capacitor bank taking the field to its floor at 0.67 per unit). Adding the drop straight is caught by slips 1.75 and 2.50.

Twelve screens: SHOW 1, 3, 5, 7, 9 alternate with DO 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, ending on two mixed puzzles (11 options, 12 typed). Every figure answer is typed with slips; options remain only for 'which needs more field'. SHOW screens are 81, 76, 74, 80 and 67 words.
The cause is visible: the drop arrow swings with I, so the along part grows on lagging and points back on leading; the AVR-off setting shows the same cause moving V instead.
Per unit is earned from his percentage impedance (per cent / 100) and tested at once (660 V, slip 6.6 V).
fix: False absolute (fault 2): 'A leading load needs less' has no comparison; 0.8 leading at rated current still needs E = 1.20, more than no load. Say 'at the same current'. Same in the rules of thumb.
False absolute (fault 2): 'It falls on a lagging load and rises on a leading one' with the AVR off is only true compared with unity at the same current. Say so.
False absolute (fault 2): screen 1's Read says the AVR must make E bigger than V; on a zero pf leading load E is smaller. Say E and V part.
Model gap: with the AVR off, E frozen at the unrounded 1.803 gives V = 0.445, which would show 0.45 against a worked 0.44. Freeze the field to the nearest whole per cent, so E holds 1.80.
Causal step thin (fault 1): why armature reaction and leakage behave as a reactance is asserted. Add that both grow with the load current.

Analogy overstates: a lagging current does not line the x drop up with the voltage; it tips it towards it. Common mistake 'It cuts the field the AVR needs' reads oddly; say the AVR must cut the field.
verdict: rewrite as draft 2 with the six fixes; no structural change
